newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN V JUVENTUS TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MILAN V JUVENTUS TACTICS.

text.p: The following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Milan and Juventus who meet in Italy's serie A at San Siro stadium on Sunday (1830 GMT):

Playing style - Started season under Uruguayan Oscar Washington Tabarez with 4-3-3. Terrible start saw Roberto Baggio dumped on to bench and a return to 4-4-2 that gave ex-coach Fabio Capello four titles in five years. Likely to be seen again on Sunday. New-old coach Arrigo Sacchi has introduced tougher training and a return to "pressing" where players work in tight spaces. Has also brought back straight back-four, the off-side trap and schemes to break down packed defences.

Strengths - George Weah can be devastating but he is absent. Paolo Maldini is ranked as one of best defenders in the world and veteran Franco Baresi is untiring. The club has clambered back from the abyss of the early season and has a run of good results behind it giving new confidence.

Weaknesses - Milan's ageing squad, most of whom are familiar with Sacchi from the national team or Milan's past, have struggled to adapt to high-intensity performances demanded by tactics. Defence was a problem at the start of the season, with Milan conceding a goal a game. Not any more, although Alessandro Costacurta is suspended on Sunday and Demetrio Albertini is doubtful after complaining of pain in a testicle.

Motivation - To finish second in the league, as the club has already announced in a declaration that caused uproar among fans used to winning. But with Juventus so far ahead in the league, and with second place bringing a European Cup place, the ambition is the most realistic one Milan can make. Beating Juve would show that Milan are back and help the above aim. Sacchi has also made no secret that there will be a purge of Milan's Old Guard at the end of the season. Those who want to stay are determined to show why they should be kept on.

Line-up (probable) - Sebastiano Rossi, Mauro Tassotti, Pietro Vierchowod, Paolo Maldini, Demetrio Albertini, Franco Baresi, Dejan Savicevic, Marcel Desailly, Zvonimir Boban, Christophe Dugarry, Marco Simone. (Roberto Baggio expected to be on bench).

Playing style - With the arrival of Frenchman Zinedine Zidane and Croat Alen Boksic, coach Marcello Lippi has refined the 4-3-3 formation that brought Juve the European Cup. He has used a 4-3-2-1 and more conservative 4-4-2. The latter is expected on Sunday against a resurgent Milan.

Strengths - Strength in depth and tactics of a coach regularly voted Italy's best. Juve's relentless harrying of opponents coupled with the ability to switch defence into attack is a threat from any part of the field.

Weaknesses - Mostly injury-related. Uruguayan Paolo Montero is on international duty and France's Didier Deschamps is suspended. Alen Boksic is not fully fit after long injury layoff but will play, Alessandro Del Piero had hoped to be back in time for this match after more than a month out but is not ready. Tiredness is a danger for Di Livio and Ferrara, twin pillars in team, after two World Cup games in five days.

Motivation - Well on course for a league and European Cup double, emulating Milan in successfully defending the European Cup. Lippi has never beaten Sacchi as a coach in their three previous encounters but this will be their first meeting with evenly-matched teams. Christian Vieri is fired up after scoring on international debut but may be tired.

Line-up (probably from) - Angelo Peruzzi; Gianluca Pessotto, Angelo Di Livio, Sergio Porrini, Ciro Ferrara, Manuel Dimas, Attilio Lombardo, Zinedine Zidane, Vladimir Jugovic, Alen Boksic, Christian Vieri.

Stefano Braschi, 39. A commercial agent from near Florence. Has been referee in serie A since 1992. Has refereed both clubs this season (Juventus-Inter, Sampdoria-Juventus and Milan-Inter). Has awarded six penalties in his last eight matches. He sent off Milan's Dutchman Edgar Davids, now injured, for an insult earlier this season and denied Juve's Alessandro Del Piero what many saw as a clear penalty.
